queries.query: maximum over sign choices of absolute signed finite sum plus a constant equals sum of absolute values plus absolute constant

results.signature:
{G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [LinearOrder G] [IsOrderedAddMonoid G] (f : ι → G) (s : Finset ι) :
  |∑ i ∈ s, f i| ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, |f i|
results.informal_description: For any additive commutative group $G$ equipped with a linear order and compatible addition (i.e., an ordered additive commutative monoid), any function $f : \iota \to G$, and any finite set $s \subseteq \iota$, the absolute value of the sum of $f(i)$ over $s$ is less than or equal to the sum of the absolute values of $f(i)$ over $s$. This generalizes the classical triangle inequality to finite sums in ordered algebraic structures.

results.signature:
[Semiring R] [Semiring S] [PartialOrder S] [IsOrderedRing S] (abv : R → S) [IsAbsoluteValue abv] (f : ι → R)
  (s : Finset ι) : abv (∑ i ∈ s, f i) ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, abv (f i)
results.informal_description: For an absolute value function $ abv : R \to S $ between semirings $ R $ and $ S $ (where $ S $ is an ordered ring), the absolute value of the sum of elements $ f(i) $ over a finite set $ s $ satisfies $ abv\left(\sum_{i \in s} f(i)\right) \leq \sum_{i \in s} abv(f(i)) $. This generalizes the triangle inequality to finite sums in ordered semirings.

results.signature: (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → ℤ) : (∑ i ∈ s, f i).natAbs ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, (f i).natAbs
results.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $ of type $ \iota $ and any function $ f : \iota \to \mathbb{Z} $, the absolute value of the sum of $ f(i) $ over $ s $ is less than or equal to the sum of the absolute values of $ f(i) $ over $ s $. Formally, $ \left| \sum_{i \in s} f(i) \right| \leq \sum_{i \in s} |f(i)| $.

results.signature: [AddCommGroup α] [LinearOrder α] [IsOrderedAddMonoid α] {s : Multiset α} : |s.sum| ≤ (s.map abs).sum

results.signature: [AddLeftMono S] (l : List R) : abv l.sum ≤ (l.map abv).sum

results.signature:

queries.query: affine span is top when differences of points span the whole vector space

results.signature: {s : Set P} (hs : s.Nonempty) : affineSpan k s = ⊤ ↔ vectorSpan k s = ⊤
results.informal_description: For a non-empty subset $ S $ of an affine space $ P $, the affine span of $ S $ equals the entire space $ P $ if and only if the vector span of $ S $ (generated by differences $ a - b $ for $ a, b \in S $) equals the entire vector space $ V $.

results.signature: {s : Set P} [Nontrivial P] : affineSpan k s = ⊤ ↔ vectorSpan k s = ⊤
results.informal_description: For a nontrivial torsor $P$ over a ring $k$, the affine span of a subset $s \subseteq P$ equals the entire space $P$ if and only if the vector span of $s$ (generated by differences $a - b$ for $a, b \in s$) equals the entire module $V$ acting on $P$.

results.signature:

  affineSpan k (Set.range p) = ⊤ ↔ Fintype.card ι = finrank k V + 1
results.informal_description: For an affinely independent family of points $ p_i $ in an affine space $ P $ over a division ring $ k $, the affine span of $ \{p_i\} $ equals the entire space $ P $ if and only if the number of points in the family is equal to the dimension of the underlying vector space $ V $ plus one.

results.signature:
{s : Set V} (p : P) (h : Submodule.span k (Set.range ((↑) : s → V)) = ⊤) :
  affineSpan k ({ p } ∪ (fun v => v +ᵥ p) '' s) = ⊤
results.informal_description: If the vector span of a set $S$ in a module $V$ equals the entire module $V$, then the affine span of the union of a singleton set $\{p\}$ and the set obtained by translating each element of $S$ by $p$ (i.e., $\{v + p \mid v \in S\}$) equals the entire affine space $P$.

results.signature: : affineSpan k (Set.univ : Set P) = ⊤
results.informal_description: The affine span of the universal set $ P $ is equal to the entire torsor $ P $, i.e., $ \operatorname{affineSpan}_k(P) = \top $. This follows from the fact that the universal set contains all points of the torsor, so its affine span must be the full space itself.

results.signature: (s : Set P) : AffineSubspace k P
results.informal_description: The affine span of a subset $ s $ of an affine space $ P $ is the smallest affine subspace containing $ s $, constructed as the set of all points obtained by adding vectors from the vector span of $ s $ (generated by differences $ a - b $ for $ a, b \in s $) to elements of $ s $. Formally, it consists of all points $ p $ such that $ p = v + p_1 $ for some $ p_1 \in s $ and $ v $ in the vector span of $ s $. This affine subspace is closed under affine combinations with coefficients in the ring $ k $ summing to 1.

results.signature: {s : Set P₁} (e : P₁ ≃ᵃ[k] P₂) : affineSpan k s = ⊤ ↔ affineSpan k (e '' s) = ⊤
results.informal_description: The collection of affine subspaces over a ring $ k $ in a torsor $ P $ forms a complete lattice. For any family of affine subspaces, their infimum (greatest lower bound) is their set-theoretic intersection, and their supremum (least upper bound) is the affine span of the union of their underlying sets. The top element is the entire torsor $ P $, and the bottom element is the empty set. This structure is valid because intersections of affine subspaces are affine subspaces, and the affine span of any subset is the smallest affine subspace containing it, ensuring closure under arbitrary meets and joins.

queries.query: continuous real function attains minimum on a nonempty compact set

queries.query: finite group representation averaging is projection onto invariant subspace

results.signature: : LinearMap.IsProj ρ.invariants ρ.averageMap
results.informal_description: The averaging map associated with a representation of a finite group over a commutative semiring, where the group's cardinality is invertible, is a linear projection operator whose image coincides with the submodule of $G$-invariant elements. This means the map satisfies $\pi \circ \pi = \pi$ and $\mathrm{im}(\pi) = V^G$.

results.signature: (v : V) : averageMap ρ v ∈ invariants ρ
results.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $k$, finite group $G$ with invertible cardinality $\#G$ in $k$, and representation $\rho: G \to \mathrm{End}_k(V)$, the image of the averaging map $v \mapsto \frac{1}{\#G} \sum_{g \in G} \rho(g)(v)$ lies in the submodule $V^G$ of $G$-invariant vectors. That is, for every $v \in V$, the averaged vector $\frac{1}{\#G} \sum_{g \in G} \rho(g)(v)$ is fixed by the action of every $g \in G$.

    [inst : CommSemiring k] → [Group G] → [inst_2 : Fintype G] → [Invertible ↑(Fintype.card G)] → MonoidAlgebra k G
results.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ k $, a finite group $ G $, and an invertible cardinality $ \#G $ in $ k $, this constructs the average element in the group algebra $ k[G] $, defined as $ \frac{1}{\#G} \sum_{g \in G} g $, where the sum is taken over all elements of $ G $ and scaled by the inverse of the group's cardinality.

results.signature: [Fintype G] {X : FDRep k G} (v : X) : (G → k) →ₗ[k] X
results.informal_description:
Let $k$ be a commutative ring and $G$ be a finite group. Let $(X, \rho)$ be a finitely generated representation of $G$ over $k$, where $\rho: G \to \mathrm{End}_k(X)$ is the group homomorphism to the endomorphism ring of $X$. For a fixed vector $v \in X$, this definition constructs a $k$-linear map from the space of functions from $G$ to $k$, denoted $(G \to k)$, to the representation space $X$. This linear map takes a function $f: G \to k$ and maps it to the vector given by the sum:
$$ \sum_{s \in G} f(s) \cdot \rho(s^{-1})(v) $$

results.signature:
{k : Type u_1} →

        [inst_1 : Group G] → [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid V] → [inst_3 : Module k V] → Representation k G V → Submodule k V
results.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $k$, group $G$, and $k$-module $V$ equipped with a representation $\rho: G \to \mathrm{End}_k(V)$, this is the submodule of $V$ consisting of all elements $v \in V$ such that $\rho(g)(v) = v$ for every $g \in G$. This submodule is denoted $V^G$ and contains precisely the elements of $V$ fixed by the entire group action.

results.signature: (hm₁ : m₁ ∈ evenOdd Q₁ 1) (hm₂ : m₂ ∈ evenOdd Q₂ 1) : map f₁ m₁ * map f₂ m₂ = -map f₂ m₂ * map f₁ m₁
results.informal_description: If $ m_1 $ and $ m_2 $ are elements in the odd subspaces of the Clifford algebras $ \mathrm{Cl}(R, M_1, Q_1) $ and $ \mathrm{Cl}(R, M_2, Q_2) $ respectively, then the images of $ m_1 $ and $ m_2 $ under the induced algebra homomorphisms $ f_1 $ and $ f_2 $ anticommute, i.e., $ f_1(m_1) \cdot f_2(m_2) = -f_2(m_2) \cdot f_1(m_1) $.

results.signature: {a b : M} (h : Q.IsOrtho a b) : ι Q a * ι Q b + ι Q b * ι Q a = 0
results.informal_description: For any elements $a, b$ in the $R$-module $M$ that are orthogonal with respect to the quadratic form $Q$ (i.e., $Q(a + b) = Q(a) + Q(b)$), the product of their images under the canonical inclusion map $\iota: M \to \mathrm{Cl}(R, M, Q)$ into the Clifford algebra satisfies $\iota(a) \iota(b) + \iota(b) \iota(a) = 0$.

results.signature: (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) {a b : M} (h : Q.IsOrtho a b) : ι Q a * (ι Q b * x) = -(ι Q b * (ι Q a * x))
results.informal_description: For any elements $a, b$ in an $R$-module $M$ that are orthogonal with respect to a quadratic form $Q$ (i.e., $Q(a + b) = Q(a) + Q(b)$), and for any element $x$ in the Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}(R, M, Q)$, the inclusion map $\iota: M \to \mathrm{Cl}(R, M, Q)$ satisfies the anticommutation relation: $\iota(a) \cdot (\iota(b) \cdot x) = -\iota(b) \cdot (\iota(a) \cdot x)$.

results.signature: (a b : M) : ι Q a * ι Q b = algebraMap R _ (QuadraticMap.polar Q a b) - ι Q b * ι Q a
results.informal_description: For any elements $ a, b $ in the $ R $-module $ M $, the product of their images under the canonical inclusion $ \iota: M \to \mathrm{Cl}(R, M, Q) $ satisfies $ \iota(a) \iota(b) = \text{algebraMap}_R(B_Q(a, b)) - \iota(b) \iota(a) $, where $ B_Q $ denotes the polar form of the quadratic form $ Q $. This expresses the fundamental anticommutation relation in the Clifford algebra generated by $ Q $.

results.signature: {a b : M} (h : Q.IsOrtho a b) : ι Q a * ι Q b = -(ι Q b * ι Q a)
results.informal_description: For any elements $a$ and $b$ in the module $M$ that are orthogonal with respect to the quadratic form $Q$, the product of their images under the canonical inclusion map $\iota: M \to \mathrm{Cl}(R, M, Q)$ satisfies $\iota(a)\iota(b) = -\iota(b)\iota(a)$.

results.signature: [Fintype α] (s : Finset α) : Gᶜ.IsMaximumClique s ↔ G.IsMaximumIndepSet s
results.informal_description: For a finite simple graph $G$ and a finite set $s$ of vertices, the set $s$ is a maximum clique in the complement graph $\overline{G}$ if and only if $s$ is a maximum independent set in the original graph $G$.

results.signature: (G : SimpleGraph V) (c : Set V) : Prop
results.informal_description: A vertex cover of a simple graph $ G $ is a set $ c $ of vertices such that for every pair of adjacent vertices $ v $ and $ w $ in $ G $, at least one of $ v $ or $ w $ is in $ c $. In other words, every edge of $ G $ has at least one endpoint in $ c $.

results.signature: [Fintype α] (s : Finset α) : Gᶜ.IsMaximumIndepSet s ↔ G.IsMaximumClique s
results.informal_description: For a simple graph $ G $ on a finite vertex set $ \alpha $, a finite set $ s $ of vertices is a maximum independent set in the complement graph $ \overline{G} $ if and only if $ s $ is a maximum clique in $ G $.

results.signature: (s : Finset α) : Maximal Gᶜ.IsIndepSet s ↔ Maximal G.IsClique s
results.informal_description: For a finite set $ s $ of vertices in a simple graph $ G $, $ s $ is a maximal independent set in the complement graph $ \overline{G} $ if and only if $ s $ is a maximal clique in the original graph $ G $.

results.signature: [Finite α] : ∃ s, G.IsNClique G.cliqueNum s
results.informal_description: In any finite simple graph $ G $, there exists a clique $ S $ such that the cardinality of $ S $ is precisely the clique number of $ G $. This asserts that the supremum defining the clique number is attained by an actual clique in the graph.

results.signature: : (∃ M : Subgraph G, M.IsPerfectMatching) ↔ ∀ u, ¬G.IsTutteViolator u
results.informal_description: A finite simple graph $ G $ admits a perfect matching if and only if for every subset $ U $ of its vertices, the number of connected components in $ G - U $ with an odd number of vertices is at most $ |U| $.
